articles.title: Putin Keeps Europe Out: Kremlin Contradicts Washington Over Ukraine Peace Talks

articles.title: EU's Kaja Kallas: Kushner Finally Admits Europe is Needed at Russia Ukraine Peace Talks | Vantage
articles.description: The European Union has finally been invited to attend Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations. US special envoy Jared Kushner says that both Moscow and Kyiv have agreed to expand the peace talks to include Brussels, after the trilateral between the US, Russia, Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. EU Foreign Policy Chief, Kaja Kallas, is likely to represent Brussels at the next talks. Firstpost looks at how Kallas reacted to the invitation from Kushner. Hem Kaur Saroya explains the comments made by Kallas which may come across as criticism of Kushner and the other US envoy, Steve Witkoff. HKS also looks at how the Kremlin is likely to react to Kallas at the next round of negotiations.

articles.title: Kremlin rules out European participation in next round of Ukraine peace talks
articles.description: Russia's position regarding European participation in Ukraine peace talks remains unchanged, according to Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov. While US negotiators suggested that Moscow was open to Europe's involvement, Ushakov contradicted this remark. He emphasized that discussions are currently focused on a trilateral format for the negotiations. Additionally, Ushakov indicated that significant steps are necessary before agreeing on European participation.
